data.title: JPMorgan Expands Tokenized Money Market Funds To Solana
data.description:
TL;DR: J.P. Morgan Asset Management says qualified U.S. investors can now access MONY and JLTXX tokenized money market funds on Solana through its Morgan Money platform.

J.P. Morgan Asset Management is bringing two of its tokenized money market funds to Solana, extending a traditional cash-management business across another public blockchain.

In an announcement Thursday, the investment manager said qualified U.S. investors can now access My OnChain Net Yield Fund, known as MONY, and the JPMorgan OnChain Liquidity–Token Money Market Fund, JLTXX, on Solana through its Morgan Money platform. Investors can subscribe and redeem through that institutional interface and receive balances represented at blockchain addresses.

Different funds, different investor rules

The two products are not identical forms of digital cash. MONY is a private placement offered under Rule 506(c), with eligibility restrictions for qualifying investors. JLTXX is a U.S.-registered government money market fund structured to serve cash management needs, including those of stablecoin issuers.

Both represent fund interests rather than ordinary deposit balances. J.P. Morgan's disclosures make clear that the funds are not bank accounts or FDIC-insured deposits, and that even products seeking a stable $1 share value can lose money.

That difference is easy to overlook when a token moves through a wallet interface. The blockchain record can make ownership and transfers more programmable; it does not change the underlying fund's investment objectives, regulatory status or redemption restrictions.

Why Solana now?

Institutions experimenting with tokenized assets increasingly operate across more than one chain. A fund that can be subscribed into on multiple networks may be more useful as a liquidity-management instrument, particularly when portfolio and treasury teams hold digital balances in different environments.

J.P. Morgan says adding Solana is intended to let clients access the same fund strategies across the networks where they operate. It is a distribution and settlement expansion, not the creation of two wholly new investment strategies.

The bank's Morgan Money platform remains central to the customer experience. That is significant because professional investors need controls that go beyond seeing a token balance, including eligibility screening, reporting, fund documents and predictable subscriptions and redemptions.

The company published Solana token addresses for both products, but copying a token identifier from social media is not a substitute for using the manager's verified onboarding channel. Token impersonation and lookalike assets remain a risk in on-chain markets.

For Solana, the listing adds another institutional financial product beyond speculative trading. For J.P. Morgan, it tests whether a familiar regulated fund structure can retain its governance while using a wider set of blockchain rails. Actual institutional adoption and transaction volumes, not the announcement alone, will show the importance of that change.

Source: www.prnewswire.com original announcement or data.

Related Reading: tokenized assets; crypto custody; stablecoins.

data.title: BP, Louisiana reach deal to accelerate Deepwater Horizon payments
data.description:
BP said Friday it reached an agreement with the state of Louisiana to provide an accelerated, lump-sum $350M payment to resolve claims over the 2010 Deepwater Horizon oil spill and settle remaining coastal zone lawsuits brought by Louisiana parishes.

Louisiana had been owed $373M ‌over ⁠the next seven years, but the state will now receive a single $350M payment under the new agreement.

"We have now disposed of ​claims and settled with all ​but ⁠one of the major defendants in these coastal cases," Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry ​said.

BP said it remains a significant energy investor in the state, where it spent $590M with Louisiana vendors and paid more than $280M in royalties and property and franchise taxes in 2025.
